newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAFRICA ORDERS CLOSURE OF AGRICULTURE CREDIT BOARD.
newsitem.headline: SAFRICA ORDERS CLOSURE OF AGRICULTURE CREDIT BOARD.

text.p: South African Deputy Agriculture Minister Thoko Didiza said on Wednesday the cabinet had approved a recommendation which would result in the closure of the Agricultural Credit Board.
"This in effect means that direct credit services through the Agricultural Credit Board will end as from August 31, 1997," she said in a statement explaining the cabinet's decision.
Didiza said farmers who were in need of credit should apply to the Land Bank, commercial banks, development or other financial institutions.

The cabinet decision, she said, was based on the principle that the state had an important role to play in securing greater access to financial services by rural people, but should not engage in direct lending.

She appealed to farmers who have debts with the Department of Agriculture in terms of the Credit Act to continue repaying their loans. The national agriculture department would wind up the debt book of the Agricultural Credit Board, she said.

Didiza also said the Land Bank's role would be extended to serve the emerging agrictural sector, adding that applications for direct production input credit to emerging entrepreneurs and land reform beneficiaries would be considered by the bank from September 1.
The current pilot programme on agricultural production loans through the use of agents would continue until August 31, 1998, she said.
